passages.text:
**Abstract.** The Stieltjes measure of every integrable minimiser of the
zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure, zero-field
Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model has full support on $[0,1)$ and a smooth
density that is strictly positive on $(0,1)$. We reconstruct OpenAI's quantitative
argument, organised around two uses of one spatial-moment inequality.
On a positive constant interval, it makes the derivative of the gradient
second moment strictly convex, contradicting the endpoint conditions
imposed by minimality. The same curvature and the bounded gradient
also exclude terminal gaps. Full support then gives moment identities and
smoothness; a local constant replacement transfers the inequality to the minimiser and
forces its density to be positive. H.-B. Chen previously proved full support
and smooth nonnegative density. We isolate the fixed-time spatial moment
and the positive margin that survives local replacement, while importing its
shape comparisons and full polynomial identity. We also derive the scalar value
identity and explain its classical optimisation consequence. For the quantum approximate
optimization algorithm (QAOA), we identify the rooted energy of a finite Gaussian
observable and the separate circuit theorem that approximates it. A further
second-moment theorem gives a measured near-optimal configuration on the same
random instance, with the circuit word fixed before the number of spins grows.
passages.rationale: The main result and the second use remain source arguments under the pure zero-field SK and integrable-minimiser hypotheses. The reconstruction genre and Chen attribution are preserved. The revised closing sentence selects algorithmic consequences as an outlook, without claiming a new theorem or a density premise for the algorithms.

passages.text: [Auffinger, Chen and Zeng (2020), Theorem 1][ACZ] proved infinite support. This need not be full support: the measure $\sum_{k\geq1}2^{-k}\delta_{1-2^{-k}}$ has infinitely many atoms and many gaps. [H.-B. Chen (2026), Theorem 1.3][Chen] subsequently proved full support and smooth nonnegative density. We follow OpenAI's quantitative proof of the support conclusion and its further strict-positivity result. The feature used twice is a lower bound valid throughout every positive constant interval of an admissible coefficient, without a minimising assumption. **Theorem 1 (full support; quantitative proof following [OpenAI (2026a), Theorem 1.1][FS]).** If $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ minimises $\mathcal P$, then $$ \operatorname{supp}\mu_\gamma=[0,1),\qquad \gamma(t_2)>\gamma(t_1)\quad(0\leq t_10$, with probability tending to one there are configurations $\sigma,\tau$ with $|R(\sigma,\tau)-\rho|<\delta$ and both energies at least $n(P_*-\eta)$. This follows from [Auffinger, Chen and Zeng (2020), Proposition 1, equation (5)][ACZ], using the Gaussian normalisation above. Our purpose is to isolate the spatial moment common to the support and density arguments, explain why it needs an integrated estimate, and identify what survives the local-replacement limit. The conclusions and the quantitative method are those of the cited sources. The proof compares two demands on a gap with two support endpoints. Minimality forces $q$ to agree with time there, with endpoint slopes at most one. On a positive constant interval a quantitative estimate makes $q'$ strictly convex, so its integral is smaller than the interval's length. This contradicts the required change in $q$. After excluding all gaps, the identity $q'=1$ supplies the equation from which the same estimate will force $\gamma'>0$. A qualitative crossing criterion already suffices for a bounded gap. The density argument needs more: an estimate for a local constant replacement that need not minimise, at a time where $q''$ need not vanish, and a positive lower bound that survives the limit. The second aim, in §5, is to follow the support identities to a finite Gaussian observable whose rooted energy a QAOA circuit approximates, then identify the additional concentration input for a measured configuration. These optimisation consequences use full support; strict density positivity is a further analytic conclusion. Readers interested in optimisation may accept Theorem 1 and continue to §5. Sections 2–4 assume Itô calculus and martingale convergence; the circuit construction is a separate imported theorem. Omitted proofs are linked to *From Parisi full support to deterministic QAOA circuits: A long reasoning record*, the [companion edition of 26 October 2026](../long/reasoning-record.md); original-source citations remain beside the imported inputs.
passages.rationale: The full-support and moment conclusions retain every original hypothesis and time quantifier. The preview identifies why local flattening needs an estimate valid away from minimisers, without a crossing premise and with a surviving positive margin. The named companion edition and its section links route omitted derivations; they do not establish semantic or formal acceptance. The prescribed-overlap consequence invokes ACZ Proposition 1 for one attained full-support minimizer in the stated Gaussian normalization. Attainment supplies that same coefficient and the Parisi formula identifies its value; no additional free minimizer premise, uniform-overlap event or efficient construction is asserted.

passages.text: This AI-assisted article reconstructs the cited analytic arguments. The integrated estimate (5), its shape hypotheses and compact-strip approximation are substantial imported inputs. OpenAI's retained [full-support formal statement][support-challenge] asserts the support and moment conclusions conditional on an admissible minimiser, and constructs its associated diffusion. A separate [scalar formal statement][value-challenge] covers value identities and finite Gaussian approximation, with minimiser and diffusion premises for those clauses. Its third clause identifies the ground-state and Parisi values from a minimiser, constructing the diffusion internally. The two formal models have not been transported into one another in this record. Neither statement includes the positive-density corollary or QAOA convergence. Their [full-support][support-lean] and [scalar][value-lean] implementations use [Lean][Lean4] and [mathlib][mathlib]. A source-bound local build of the Support implementation completed on 26 October 2026, and dependency extraction recorded its conditional full-support root. Dependencies outside the selected extraction scope remain boundaries. Comparator acceptance and the scalar-target results remain pending. Exact versions, checking outcomes and correspondence are retained in the long record's [§12, “What the formal statements establish”](../long/reasoning-record.md#formal-interfaces) and [§13, “Source checks and finite calculation”](../long/reasoning-record.md#verification).
